newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to close Michigan steel wheel plant.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to close Michigan steel wheel plant.

text.p: Hayes Wheels International Inc. said Friday it will close its Romulus, Mich., manufacturing plant in 1997, affecting about 435 employees, including 60 salaried and 375 hourly workers.
Production is expected to cease in late 1997, with the total shutdown of the plant completed by the end of the year.
"The decision was based on the company's continuing efforts to rationalise excess steel wheel capacity and reduce costs resulting from current market trends," Hayes said.
The 45-year-old plant makes steel and fabricated aluminum wheels for North American original equipment manufacturers.
Over the past decade, use of aluminum wheels on North American vehicles has increased to 43 percent from 12 percent, the company said.

"The Romulus plant's steel wheel production dropped significantly during that same timeframe, which resulted in the Romulus plant operating at less than 40 percent of its potential capacity during 1996," Hayes said.
Hayes' stock was unchanged at $19.75 early on Nasdaq.
